title: Core-stable coalitions
description: A partition of agents into coalitions is core-stable if no group would all be strictly better off as a coalition of their own; existence is Sigma-2-complete for additive values (Woeginger). The abstraction guesses a partition and the check a blocking coalition. relevant/1 marks only the changes that could make a member of the blocking coalition happier where it is: losing a companion it dislikes, or gaining one it likes.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The agents and how they value each other. Added to every solver.
fragments.text: % The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): partitions of the agents.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a partition, given by tog(I,J) for agents I < J in the same coalition.
{ tog(I,J) } :- agent(I), agent(J), I < J.
same(I,J) :- tog(I,J).
same(J,I) :- tog(I,J).
:- same(I,J), same(J,K), I < K, not same(I,K).
% Shown as in(I,R): agent I is in the coalition whose smallest member is R.
first(R) :- agent(R), not same(R,J) : agent(J), J < R.
in(R,R) :- first(R).
in(I,R) :- first(R), same(I,R).
#show in/2.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: which pairs of agents are together.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for a blocking coalition (solver C).
fragments.text:
same(I,J) :- tog(I,J).
same(J,I) :- tog(I,J).
% A counterexample: a group of agents each of whom values the group strictly more
% than its present coalition.
1 { s(I) : agent(I) }.
:- s(I), #sum { V,J : s(J), value(I,J,V) ; -V,J : same(I,J), value(I,J,V) } <= 0.
#show s/1.

% The group keeps blocking unless a member becomes happier where it is. Only two
% kinds of change can do that:
% a companion the member dislikes leaves its coalition ...
help(I,J) :- s(I), same(I,J), value(I,J,V), V < 0.
% ... or an agent the member likes joins it.
help(I,J) :- s(I), agent(J), I != J, not same(I,J), value(I,J,V), V > 0.
relevant(tog(I,J)) :- help(I,J), I < J.
relevant(tog(J,I)) :- help(I,J), J < I.

fragments.name: check_members
fragments.text:
same(I,J) :- tog(I,J).
same(J,I) :- tog(I,J).
% A counterexample: a group of agents each of whom values the group strictly more
% than its present coalition.
1 { s(I) : agent(I) }.
:- s(I), #sum { V,J : s(J), value(I,J,V) ; -V,J : same(I,J), value(I,J,V) } <= 0.
#show s/1.

% A coarser refinement: the group keeps blocking as long as the coalitions of its members
% stay as they are; every pair with a member in it is blamed.
relevant(tog(I,J)) :- s(I), agent(J), I < J.
relevant(tog(J,I)) :- s(I), agent(J), J < I.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% Six agents form coalitions. value(I,J,V): agent I values being with agent J at V;
% a coalition is worth the sum over its other members.
agent(1..6).
value(1,2,-2). value(1,3,-3). value(1,4,1).  value(1,5,-3). value(1,6,4).
value(2,1,4).  value(2,3,4).  value(2,4,3).  value(2,5,-1). value(2,6,-3).
value(3,1,4).  value(3,2,-4). value(3,4,3).  value(3,5,3).  value(3,6,-4).
value(4,1,4).  value(4,2,1).  value(4,3,-1). value(4,5,-3). value(4,6,2).
value(5,1,-4). value(5,2,-4). value(5,3,-4). value(5,4,5).  value(5,6,-4).
value(6,1,3).  value(6,2,-1). value(6,3,3).  value(6,4,-4). value(6,5,5).

% Four agents whose game has an empty core: every partition is blocked.
agent(1..4).
value(1,2,-2). value(1,3,-5). value(1,4,6).
value(2,1,-3). value(2,3,5). value(2,4,6).
value(3,1,3). value(3,2,1). value(3,4,6).
value(4,1,6). value(4,2,5). value(4,3,3).

% Five agents with four core-stable partitions.
agent(1..5).
value(1,3,5). value(1,4,3). value(1,5,4).
value(2,1,2). value(2,3,5). value(2,4,-4). value(2,5,3).
value(3,1,-1). value(3,2,2). value(3,4,2). value(3,5,-2).
value(4,1,1). value(4,2,4). value(4,3,1). value(4,5,-3).
value(5,1,3). value(5,2,4). value(5,3,-3). value(5,4,-2).

% Four agents who all like each other: only the grand coalition is stable.
agent(1..4).
value(I,J,1) :- agent(I), agent(J), I != J.

generators.name: additive
generators.description: Random additive values: agent I values agent J at an integer in -m..m, uniformly and independently.
generators.text:
% additive: n agents, value(I,J,V) with V uniform in -m..m (a value 0 is left out).
agent(1..n).
val(I,J,@int(-m, m, I, J)) :- agent(I), agent(J), I != J.
value(I,J,V) :- val(I,J,V), V != 0.
#show agent/1.  #show value/3.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

loop:
    M = A.solve()
    if not M: stop
    X = C.solve(assume G(M))
    if X:
        A.add(G.clause(M, X))
    else:
        accept M
        A.add(G.block(M))

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 5):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction   options "--enum-mode=record"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

spaces.name: games
spaces.description: Additive hedonic games with size agents and values -1, 0, 1 (from 2 agents: one agent has no pair).
spaces.text:
% every additive hedonic game with the agents 1..size and values -1..1
agent(1..size).
1 { value(I,J,V) : V = -1..1 } 1 :- agent(I), agent(J), I != J.
